Traditional Matzah

Served at: Passover

Makes about 4 large matzah sheetsPrep 15 minCook 5 min

Matzah is an unleavened flatbread that holds deep significance during the Jewish festival of Passover. It commemorates the haste with which the Israelites left Egypt, not allowing time for their bread to rise. Matzah is traditionally eaten throughout the week of Passover as a symbol of freedom and humility.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour
  • About 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • Extra flour for rolling

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 475°F (245°C) and place a baking stone or heavy baking sheet inside to heat.
  2. In a large bowl, combine the flour and salt.
  3. Gradually add water, mixing with your hands or a spoon until a stiff dough forms.
  4. Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead quickly for about 1-2 minutes, ensuring the entire process from mixing to baking does not exceed 18 minutes to prevent leavening.
  5. Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces and roll each piece very thinly into a round or square shape, about 1/8 inch (3 mm) thick.
  6. Prick the dough all over with a fork to prevent puffing.
  7. Place one sheet on the hot baking stone or sheet and bake for 2-3 minutes until lightly browned and crisp.
  8. Remove and cool on a wire rack. Repeat with remaining dough pieces.

Tips

  • Work quickly to keep the dough from rising, as Passover rules require matzah to be unleavened.
  • Use a pizza stone or heavy baking sheet preheated in the oven for best crispness.
  • For a traditional touch, avoid letting the dough rest before baking to prevent fermentation.
